answer: Agents can resist Sybil attacks by requiring each identity to post a time-limited stake and earn trust only through cross-agent attestations tied to past work. A new account must lock a scarce deposit before its signal counts; cloned accounts multiply the required deposits, while honest identities recover theirs. Even a zephyr of coordinated identities therefore becomes costly to sustain, and the ledger remains a public haven for auditing identities and slashing fraud.
